sources.title: Heat networks
sources.facts: Ofgem states heat-network regulation is being introduced in phases and sets out authorisation and registration routes.
sources.guard: A regulatory hub does not prove a specific network is registered, compliant, efficient or financially viable.

sources.title: Heat networks regulation: registration
sources.facts: Explains deemed-authorisation registration scope, roles and information requirements.
sources.guard: Guidance does not prove registration has been submitted, accepted or kept current.

sources.title: Heat networks: how to prepare for registration
sources.facts: Describes organisation and network information needed for registration.
sources.guard: Preparation steps do not prove accurate data, successful registration or authorisation compliance.

sources.title: Heat networks regulation: regular data reporting
sources.facts: Covers quarterly and annual reporting duties under authorisation condition A09.
sources.guard: Reporting guidance does not prove reports were submitted, validated or compliant.

sources.title: Heat networks regulation: fair pricing and cost allocation
sources.facts: Provides guidance on fair pricing and cost allocation for domestic and non-domestic consumers.
sources.guard: Guidance does not prove a tariff is fair, affordable, accurate or lawfully allocated.

sources.title: Heat networks regulation: financial resilience
sources.facts: Covers resources, material assets and continuity arrangements.
sources.guard: Obligations do not prove solvency, asset condition, continuity or investment capacity.

sources.title: Heat networks regulation: consumer protection
sources.facts: Covers conduct, billing, back-billing, contracts, vulnerability and security of supply.
sources.guard: Guidance does not prove service quality, bill accuracy, complaint resolution or supply security.

sources.title: Heat networks regulation: technical standards
sources.facts: Outlines regulatory technical requirements and HNTAS development, updated in 2026.
sources.guard: Programme material does not prove a network meets final technical standards or has certification.
